readerTitle: Opening day is set by one chain of tasks
caseNote: 가상 사례 (소매점 2호점 오픈, 지역 물류센터 이전) · 모든 일정과 수치는 설명용
insight: 새 매장 오픈 날짜는 할 일 목록 전체가 아니라 서로 이어진 한 줄의 작업이 정한다. 위험은 큰 오픈 하루에 몰지 말고 작은 단계로 나눠 일찍 드러낸다.
misconception: 늦어진 일은 다 똑같이 급하고, 오픈은 첫날 한 번에 크게 해야 한다.

sources.text: 프로젝트 관리의 표준 개념 (주공정 경로, 여유 시간, 단계적 출시)
모든 일정과 수치는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 주공정 일정 계산: 인테리어 공사 1~4주, 전기 검사 5주, 소방 점검 6주, 상품 입고·진열 7~8주, 9주 차 첫날 오픈 = 총 8주. 공사가 1주 늦으면 뒤 작업이 모두 밀려 10주 차 오픈이 됩니다.
여유 시간 계산: 선반은 4주 차 말 도착 예정, 7주 차 진열에 필요하므로 여유 2주. 2주 늦어도 6주 차 말 도착으로 오픈 날짜에 영향 없음. 직원 채용은 대체 채용에 약 3주, 8주 차 교육 전까지 완료 가능.
소방 점검 예약 기간, 검사 절차는 나라와 지역마다 다릅니다. 카드에는 특정 법규가 아닌 일반적인 예시로만 썼습니다.
물류센터 사례: 컨베이어 설치가 2주 늦어지는 상황은 가상 예시입니다. 수작업 피킹으로 한 노선 먼저 시작하면 첫 단계가 컨베이어에 묶이지 않는다는 논리만 설명합니다.

cards.title: Opening day is set by one chain of tasks
body: Maya runs a successful home-goods shop. She has signed a lease for a second store and announced the opening: eight weeks from today.
Her task list has 40 items, from paint colors to the fire inspection. Three weeks in, some tasks start running late. They don't all matter equally.

image.label: Empty shop under renovation with a long task list on the wall
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 공사 중인 빈 매장, 벽에 붙은 긴 할 일 목록 종이. 창문에 "Opening soon" 표지. 실제 브랜드 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Three things slip in one week.
body: The builder says the fit-out will finish a week late. The shelving supplier says delivery is two weeks late. One new hire quits before starting.
Shelves aren't needed until setup in week 7. Staff training is in week 8. Which problem threatens opening day?

options.text: The shelving, because it's the longest delay
options.feedback: Two weeks sounds worst, but the shelves had two weeks of spare time. They still arrive before setup. Spending energy here leaves the real threat alone.

options.text: The fit-out, because the inspections can't start until it's done
options.feedback: This is the **critical path** at work. Electrical checks, the fire inspection and setup all wait on the builder, so one lost week moves opening day by one week.

options.text: The new hire, because trained staff are hard to find
options.feedback: Worth acting on soon, but a replacement can be hired and trained in the five weeks left. It only becomes urgent if that spare time runs out.

cards.title: Four tasks that wait on each other.
body: Each task starts only when the one before it ends. Together they fill all eight weeks, with no spare time. Shelving and hiring run alongside and have room to slip.

cards.title: Protect the longest chain first.
body: The **critical path** is the longest chain of tasks that depend on each other. It sets the earliest possible finish date.

For Maya, that means calling the builder today. Can a second crew work weekends? Can she book the inspector for the earliest slot after sign-off? Each day saved on the chain is a day saved on opening.
Then she checks the chain again every week, because a side task that slips too far can become the new critical path.

image.label: Timeline with one highlighted chain and shorter side bars
image.brief: 간트 차트 스타일 타임라인. 공사 → 전기 검사 → 소방 점검 → 진열로 이어지는 한 줄은 진한 색으로 강조. 선반 배송, 채용은 옅은 색 막대로 옆에 두고 뒤쪽에 "spare time" 빈 칸 표시.

cards.title: How should the store open?
body: The inspection passes. Maya has a local newspaper ad ready and a ribbon-cutting planned. The till system and staff are brand new.

options.text: Full grand opening on day one, with ads and a crowd
options.feedback: Maximum buzz, but every untested part meets its biggest test at once. A frozen till or confused staff happens in front of the most people.

options.text: A quiet week for neighbors and regulars, then the grand opening
options.feedback: This is **small steps vs big bang**. Problems show up while the stakes are small, and she fixes them before the crowd arrives.

options.text: Wait to open until everything feels perfect
options.feedback: Fewer surprises, but rent is already running, and some problems only appear with real customers. Waiting doesn't find them.

cards.title: Cheap mistakes instead of public ones.
body: In the soft-opening week, the card reader drops connection near the back wall. The checkout line blocks the front door. One product nobody can find sells out on day two.
Each fix takes an afternoon. On grand-opening day with a crowd, each would have been a bad first impression.
cards.softwareNote: Software teams do the same with a beta or a release to 5% of users first. Bugs reach a few people who expect them, not every customer at once.

cards.title: Small steps and short paths have costs.
body: Some steps can't be split. An inspection passes or it doesn't, so it stays on the chain no matter what.
A soft opening costs a week of rent with fewer sales, and early visitors still form opinions. Keep it short and invite people who will forgive rough edges.
And speeding up the critical path often costs money, like weekend crews. Pay it only when the later date costs more.

cards.title: Now it's a new warehouse.
body: A food distributor is moving to a bigger regional warehouse. The plan: switch all 12 delivery routes the day the new conveyor system is finished. The conveyor supplier now says it's two weeks late.
What should the operations manager do?

options.text: Push the full switch back two weeks and keep the plan
options.feedback: Safe and simple, but it keeps the conveyor on the critical path and still puts all 12 routes at risk on one day.

options.text: Start one route now with hand picking, add routes as the conveyor comes online
options.feedback: Moving in **small steps** takes the conveyor off the **critical path** for the first stage. The team learns the new building on one route before the rest arrive.

options.text: Switch all routes on the original date with hand picking
options.feedback: The date holds, but hand picking for 12 routes in an unfamiliar building is a big bang with no test run. Late deliveries hit every customer at once.

cards.softwareNote: A big system migration works the same way: move one team or one customer group first, while the rest stays on the old system.

cards.title: Guard the chain, then open in steps.
body: Two ideas from this unit did the work. The **critical path** showed which delay moves opening day. **Small steps vs big bang** turned launch day into a series of cheap tests.
**Try it today:** take your next project and circle the tasks that must wait for another task. Is the longest chain the one you're watching most closely?
